events.title: The Millennium Bug Fizzles
events.body: After years of warnings and billions spent on fixes, computers around the world tick over into 2000 with only minor glitches. Whether the work prevented disaster or the danger was overstated is still argued.

events.title: The Dot-com Bubble Peaks
events.body: America's tech-heavy NASDAQ index hits its high. Within two years it loses most of its value, and hundreds of internet start-ups go under.

events.title: Mozambique Floods
events.body: Weeks of rain and a cyclone flood southern Mozambique. Hundreds die and hundreds of thousands lose their homes; one woman gives birth in a tree while waiting for rescue.

events.title: Putin Elected President
events.body: Three months after Yeltsin hands him power, Vladimir Putin wins Russia's presidential election in the first round. He will dominate Russian politics for the rest of the century so far.

events.title: The ILOVEYOU Virus
events.body: An email with the subject "ILOVEYOU" spreads from the Philippines to millions of computers in days, deleting files as it goes — one of the most damaging computer worms ever released.

events.title: Tate Modern Opens
events.body: A disused power station on London's South Bank reopens as Tate Modern. Its vast Turbine Hall becomes one of the world's most visited spaces for modern art.

events.title: The Human Genome Drafted
events.body: The public Human Genome Project and the private company Celera jointly announce a first draft of the full human genetic code.

events.title: Persepolis
events.body: Marjane Satrapi begins her graphic memoir of growing up in Tehran through the revolution and the war with Iraq, published first in French in Paris. It becomes a classic and later an animated film.

events.title: Mexico Votes Out the PRI
events.body: Vicente Fox wins Mexico's presidential election, ending 71 years of unbroken rule by the Institutional Revolutionary Party.

events.title: The Durban AIDS Conference
events.body: The International AIDS Conference meets in Africa for the first time. Amid South African government doubts about the cause of AIDS, scientists, activists and Nelson Mandela call for treatment for all.

events.title: Concorde Crashes
events.body: An Air France Concorde catches fire on take-off from Paris and crashes into a hotel in Gonesse, killing 113. It is the supersonic jet's only fatal crash.

events.title: The Kursk Sinks
events.body: The Russian nuclear submarine Kursk sinks in the Barents Sea after explosions on board. All 118 crew die; Moscow is criticised for refusing foreign help for days.

events.title: Cathy Freeman's 400 Metres
events.body: Aboriginal athlete Cathy Freeman, who lit the Olympic flame, wins the 400 metres at the Sydney Games — a moment many Australians link to reconciliation.

events.title: The Second Intifada Begins
events.body: Ariel Sharon's visit to Jerusalem's Temple Mount, or Haram al-Sharif, sparks protests that grow into a Palestinian uprising lasting more than four years.

events.title: The First Crew Moves Into the ISS
events.body: An American and two Russians arrive on the International Space Station. People have lived aboard it without a break ever since.

events.title: Bush v. Gore
events.body: The US Supreme Court stops a recount in Florida, settling the presidential election for George W. Bush by a few hundred votes in that state.

events.title: Wikipedia Launches
events.body: A free encyclopedia anyone can edit goes online. Within a few years it is one of the most used websites on Earth — and the source behind much of Weft.

events.title: The Gujarat Earthquake
events.body: A powerful earthquake strikes Gujarat on India's Republic Day, flattening much of Bhuj and killing about 20,000 people.

events.title: The Bamiyan Buddhas Destroyed
events.body: The Taliban blow up two giant Buddhas carved into a cliff in central Afghanistan some 1,500 years ago, despite pleas from around the world.

events.title: Same-Sex Marriage in the Netherlands
events.body: The Netherlands becomes the first country to let same-sex couples marry. Four couples wed in Amsterdam just after midnight.

events.title: The September 11 Attacks
events.body: Al-Qaeda hijackers fly airliners into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon; a fourth plane crashes in Pennsylvania. Nearly 3,000 people die, and the world changes course.

events.title: War in Afghanistan Begins
events.body: The United States and its allies attack Afghanistan to remove the Taliban and hunt al-Qaeda. The war will last almost twenty years.

sources.title: U.S., Britain attack targets in Afghanistan (7 October 2001)
The strikes begin (7 October 2001)

events.title: The iPod
events.body: Apple launches a pocket music player promising "1,000 songs in your pocket". With iTunes, it reshapes how the world buys and carries music.

events.title: Enron Collapses
events.body: The Texas energy giant files for bankruptcy after years of hidden losses and accounting fraud, wiping out employees' savings and its auditor, Arthur Andersen.

events.title: China Joins the WTO
events.body: China becomes a member of the World Trade Organization, opening the way for its rise as the workshop of the world.

events.title: Argentina's Economy Collapses
events.body: Riots and pot-banging protests erupt as Argentina freezes bank accounts during a deep debt crisis. Within two weeks the country has five presidents and defaults on its debt.

events.title: Euro Notes and Coins Arrive
events.body: Twelve European countries swap their marks, francs, lire and pesetas for euro cash — the biggest currency changeover in history.

events.title: Angola's War Ends
events.body: Rebel leader Jonas Savimbi is killed in battle. Within six weeks a ceasefire ends Angola's civil war, which began at independence in 1975.

events.title: East Timor Becomes Independent
events.body: After a quarter-century of Indonesian occupation and a bloody 1999 vote, East Timor becomes the first new country of the 21st century.

events.title: Israel Begins the West Bank Barrier
events.body: Israel starts building a barrier of walls and fences along and inside the West Bank, saying it is to stop attacks. Palestinians call it a land grab; the International Court of Justice later rules parts of it illegal.

events.title: Brazil Win a Fifth World Cup
events.body: At the first World Cup held in Asia, hosted by South Korea and Japan, Brazil beat Germany 2–0 in Yokohama, with both goals from Ronaldo.

events.title: The International Criminal Court Opens
events.body: A permanent court to try genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity comes into being in The Hague.

events.title: The African Union Is Born
events.body: Leaders meeting in Durban launch the African Union, replacing the Organisation of African Unity with a body that can step in to stop genocide and war crimes.

events.title: The Johannesburg Earth Summit
events.body: Ten years after Rio, world leaders meet in Johannesburg for the World Summit on Sustainable Development, on water, energy and poverty.

events.title: The Bali Bombings
events.body: Bombs in the tourist district of Kuta kill 202 people, many of them Australian. An al-Qaeda-linked group, Jemaah Islamiyah, is blamed.

events.title: The Moscow Theatre Siege
events.body: Chechen fighters take about 850 people hostage during a musical in Moscow. Russian forces pump gas into the building to end the siege; more than 130 hostages die.

events.title: Lula Elected
events.body: Former metalworker and union leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's presidency at his fourth attempt.

events.title: SARS Appears
events.body: A new and deadly respiratory virus emerges in southern China. By mid-2003 it has spread to some 30 countries before being contained.

events.title: Columbia Breaks Up
events.body: The space shuttle Columbia disintegrates over Texas as it returns to Earth, killing its crew of seven, including Israel's first astronaut.

events.title: The World Says No to War
events.body: Millions of people in hundreds of cities march against the coming invasion of Iraq — often called the largest protest in history.

events.title: War in Darfur
events.body: Rebels in western Sudan rise against the government, which answers with bombing and the Janjaweed militias. Hundreds of thousands die; the US later calls it genocide.

events.title: The Invasion of Iraq
events.body: American, British and allied forces invade Iraq without UN approval, citing weapons of mass destruction that are never found.

sources.title: The strikes begin (20 March 2003)
On this day: when the US first invaded Iraq in 2003

events.title: Baghdad Falls
events.body: US troops help pull down Saddam Hussein's statue in Baghdad's Firdos Square, an image broadcast around the world.

events.title: The Human Genome Completed
events.body: The Human Genome Project announces it has finished sequencing human DNA, two years ahead of schedule.

events.title: The Kite Runner
events.body: Khaled Hosseini's first novel follows two Afghan boys from the last peaceful years of the monarchy through the Soviet invasion and Taliban rule. It becomes a worldwide bestseller.

events.title: Liberia's War Ends
events.body: Warlord-president Charles Taylor steps down and goes into exile as rebels close in. Liberian women's mass protests for peace, led by Leymah Gbowee, helped force the talks.

events.title: The European Heatwave
events.body: The hottest summer Europe had recorded kills tens of thousands of people, many of them elderly and alone, with France worst hit.

events.title: China Sends a Man Into Space
events.body: Yang Liwei orbits the Earth fourteen times in Shenzhou 5, making China the third country to launch a person into space on its own.

events.title: Concorde's Last Flight
events.body: British Airways flies Concorde for the last time, from New York to London. Supersonic passenger travel ends.

events.title: Georgia's Rose Revolution
events.body: Protesters carrying roses storm parliament in Tbilisi after a disputed election, and President Eduard Shevardnadze resigns.

events.title: Saddam Hussein Captured
events.body: American soldiers find the former Iraqi leader hiding in a hole near his home town of Tikrit.

events.title: Spirit Lands on Mars
events.body: NASA's rover Spirit bounces to a landing on Mars; its twin, Opportunity, follows three weeks later and keeps working for fourteen years.

events.title: Super Size Me
events.body: Morgan Spurlock eats only McDonald's for a month and films what happens to his body. The documentary turns fast food into a public-health argument.

events.title: Facebook Launches
events.body: Harvard student Mark Zuckerberg launches "TheFacebook" for fellow students. Within a decade it connects more than a billion people.

events.title: The Madrid Train Bombings
events.body: Bombs on four commuter trains in Madrid kill 193 people, days before a Spanish election.

events.title: The Abu Ghraib Photographs
events.body: Photographs taken by American guards showing the abuse and humiliation of Iraqi prisoners at Abu Ghraib prison are made public.

events.title: Europe Grows by Ten
events.body: Ten countries, most of them formerly behind the Iron Curtain, join the European Union in its largest single expansion.

events.title: Graphene Isolated
events.body: At the University of Manchester, Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov peel single-atom-thick sheets of carbon off graphite using sticky tape. The discovery wins the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics.

events.title: The Olympics Return to Athens
events.body: The Summer Olympics return to Greece, home of the ancient Games and of the first modern Olympics in 1896.

events.title: The Beslan School Siege
events.body: Chechen separatists seize a school in Beslan on the first day of term. The siege ends in explosions and gunfire three days later; more than 330 people die, over half of them children.

events.title: Wangari Maathai Wins the Nobel
events.body: Kenyan environmentalist Wangari Maathai, whose Green Belt Movement planted tens of millions of trees, becomes the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

events.title: Yasser Arafat Dies
events.body: The Palestinian leader dies in a hospital near Paris after nearly four decades at the head of the Palestinian national movement.

events.title: Ukraine's Orange Revolution
events.body: Hundreds of thousands of people in orange fill Kyiv to protest a rigged presidential election. A re-run vote in December is won by Viktor Yushchenko.

events.title: World of Warcraft
events.body: An online fantasy game launches; within a few years more than ten million people around the world are paying to play it together.

events.title: Hotel Rwanda
events.body: Terry George's film tells the story of hotel manager Paul Rusesabagina sheltering more than a thousand people during the genocide, bringing Rwanda's 1994 horror to a global audience.

events.title: The Indian Ocean Tsunami
events.body: An undersea earthquake off Sumatra sends waves across the Indian Ocean, killing about 230,000 people in fourteen countries, from Indonesia to Somalia.

events.title: Taipei 101 Opens
events.body: Taiwan's bamboo-shaped tower opens as the world's tallest building, with a giant steel ball inside to steady it against typhoons and earthquakes.

events.title: The Kyoto Protocol Takes Effect
events.body: The first international treaty to cut greenhouse gas emissions comes into force, though the United States, then the biggest emitter, has not ratified it.

sources.title: Kyoto Protocol enters into force (2005 press release)
Kyoto enters into force (9 February 2005)

events.title: Pope John Paul II Dies
events.body: The Polish pope dies after 26 years in office. Millions travel to Rome; Joseph Ratzinger is elected Pope Benedict XVI seventeen days later.

events.title: The First YouTube Video
events.body: Co-founder Jawed Karim uploads "Me at the zoo", nineteen seconds at San Diego Zoo. Within two years, YouTube is the world's video stage.

events.title: Botero's Abu Ghraib
events.body: Colombian painter Fernando Botero, known for his round, gentle figures, paints a series of large works on the abuse of prisoners at Abu Ghraib, and refuses to sell them.

events.title: Live 8
events.body: Twenty years after Live Aid, concerts in ten cities, including Johannesburg, call on the G8 to cancel the debts of the poorest countries.

events.title: The London Bombings
events.body: Suicide bombers attack three Underground trains and a bus during the morning rush hour, killing 52 people.

events.title: Banksy Paints the West Bank Wall
events.body: Banksy paints scenes on the Israeli barrier around Bethlehem — children with buckets and spades, a ladder over the wall, a window onto a beach.

events.title: Hurricane Katrina
events.body: Katrina strikes the US Gulf Coast. Levees fail and flood most of New Orleans; more than 1,300 people die and the slow response becomes a national scandal.

events.title: The Kashmir Earthquake
events.body: An earthquake centred near Muzaffarabad kills more than 80,000 people in Pakistan and India, many of them children in collapsed schools.

events.title: Africa Elects a Woman President
events.body: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf wins Liberia's presidential run-off, two years after the civil war ended. She becomes Africa's first elected female head of state.

events.title: Merkel Becomes Chancellor
events.body: Angela Merkel, raised in communist East Germany, becomes Germany's first woman chancellor. She will serve sixteen years.

events.title: Evo Morales Elected
events.body: Coca farmers' leader Evo Morales wins Bolivia's presidential election outright, becoming the country's first Indigenous president.

events.title: Michelle Bachelet Takes Office
events.body: A doctor once detained and exiled under Pinochet becomes Chile's first woman president.

events.title: The First Tweet
events.body: Jack Dorsey posts "just setting up my twttr". Twitter becomes a newswire, a protest tool and a battleground.

events.title: Montenegro Becomes Independent
events.body: Montenegro declares independence after a referendum, ending the last remnant of Yugoslavia.

events.title: An Inconvenient Truth
events.body: Al Gore's slideshow on climate change becomes a hit documentary and wins an Oscar, carrying global warming into mainstream conversation.

events.title: Half of a Yellow Sun
events.body: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's novel of the Nigerian civil war, told through a houseboy, a professor's lover and an English writer, wins the Orange Prize.

events.title: Zidane's Headbutt
events.body: In his last match, France's Zinedine Zidane is sent off for headbutting an Italian defender in the World Cup final in Berlin. Italy win on penalties.

events.title: The Lebanon War
events.body: Hezbollah captures two Israeli soldiers; Israel answers with a month-long air and ground war in Lebanon. More than a thousand Lebanese die, most of them civilians.

events.title: Pluto Demoted
events.body: Astronomers meeting in Prague define "planet" for the first time — and Pluto no longer qualifies. The solar system has eight planets.

events.title: North Korea's First Nuclear Test
events.body: North Korea explodes a nuclear device underground, the eighth country to test one.

events.title: A Nobel for Small Loans
events.body: Muhammad Yunus and his Grameen Bank win the Nobel Peace Prize for lending tiny sums to poor people, mostly women, in Bangladesh.

events.title: The Wii
events.body: Nintendo's console with a motion-sensing controller gets grandparents bowling in their living rooms.

events.title: Saddam Hussein Executed
events.body: Iraq's former leader is hanged in Baghdad after being convicted of crimes against humanity. A leaked phone video of the hanging causes outrage.

events.title: The iPhone
events.body: Steve Jobs unveils "an iPod, a phone and an internet communicator" in one device. The smartphone age begins.

events.title: Persepolis, the Film
events.body: Marjane Satrapi's graphic memoir becomes a black-and-white animated film. It shares the Jury Prize at Cannes; Iran protests.

events.title: The Last Harry Potter
events.body: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows sells millions of copies on its first day, closing a series that turned a generation into readers.

events.title: The Run on Northern Rock
events.body: Savers queue outside Northern Rock branches to pull their money out — Britain's first bank run in over a century and an early sign of the global financial crisis.

events.title: The Saffron Revolution
events.body: Thousands of Buddhist monks march through Myanmar's cities against military rule. The junta crushes the protests.

events.title: A Nobel for Climate Science
events.body: The UN's climate panel, the IPCC, and Al Gore share the Nobel Peace Prize for warning the world about climate change.

events.title: Benazir Bhutto Assassinated
events.body: The former prime minister of Pakistan is killed by a gun and bomb attack after an election rally in Rawalpindi.

events.title: Kenya Erupts After the Election
events.body: A disputed presidential result sets off weeks of ethnic violence in Kenya. More than 1,100 people die before a power-sharing deal in February.

events.title: Kosovo Declares Independence
events.body: Kosovo breaks away from Serbia nine years after the NATO bombing campaign. Many countries recognise it; Serbia and Russia do not.

events.title: Fidel Castro Steps Down
events.body: After nearly half a century in power, an ailing Fidel Castro hands the presidency of Cuba to his brother Raúl.

events.title: The Food Price Riots
events.body: World prices of rice, wheat and maize soar. Protests and riots break out in more than thirty countries, from Haiti to Egypt to Bangladesh.

events.title: Cyclone Nargis
events.body: A cyclone floods Myanmar's Irrawaddy Delta, killing about 138,000 people. The military government at first blocks foreign aid.

events.title: Xenophobic Violence in South Africa
events.body: Attacks on foreign Africans spread from Alexandra in Johannesburg across the country. More than sixty people die and tens of thousands are displaced.

events.title: The Sichuan Earthquake
events.body: An earthquake in Sichuan kills almost 70,000 people, among them thousands of children in poorly built schools.

events.title: The "Hope" Poster
events.body: Street artist Shepard Fairey's red, beige and blue portrait of Barack Obama becomes the defining image of the campaign.

events.title: Waltz with Bashir
events.body: Israeli director Ari Folman's animated documentary pieces together his lost memories of the 1982 Lebanon war and the Sabra and Shatila massacre.

events.title: Zimbabwe's Hyperinflation
events.body: Zimbabwe's inflation runs into the billions of per cent; by early 2009 the central bank is issuing a 100-trillion-dollar note, and the country abandons its own currency.

events.title: The Beijing Olympics
events.body: China opens its first Olympic Games with a spectacular ceremony. Michael Phelps wins a record eight gold medals and Usain Bolt breaks the world records for 100 and 200 metres.

events.title: The Russia–Georgia War
events.body: Fighting over South Ossetia becomes a five-day war in which Russian forces push deep into Georgia.

events.title: The Large Hadron Collider Starts
events.body: The first proton beam circles CERN's 27-kilometre collider under the French–Swiss border, the largest machine ever built.

events.title: Lehman Brothers Collapses
events.body: The fourth-largest American investment bank goes bankrupt. Panic spreads through the world's banks, and the global financial crisis begins in earnest.

sources.title: Lehman files for bankruptcy, plans to sell units (15 September 2008)
Lehman files for biggest bankruptcy in U.S. after suitors balk

events.title: The Bitcoin White Paper
events.body: Someone calling themselves Satoshi Nakamoto publishes a nine-page plan for "a peer-to-peer electronic cash system". Their identity is still unknown.

events.title: Obama Elected
events.body: Barack Obama is elected the first Black president of the United States.

events.title: Miriam Makeba Dies
events.body: 'Mama Africa', the singer exiled for thirty years for speaking against apartheid, collapses and dies after a concert in Italy.

events.title: The Mumbai Attacks
events.body: Ten gunmen from Pakistan attack hotels, a railway station, a café and a Jewish centre in Mumbai over four days, killing about 166 people.

events.title: The Miracle on the Hudson
events.body: Geese knock out both engines of an Airbus leaving New York; Captain Sullenberger glides it down onto the Hudson River, and all 155 people survive.

events.title: Obama Sworn In
events.body: Barack Obama is inaugurated before a crowd of well over a million in Washington.

events.title: Minecraft
events.body: A Swedish programmer releases an early version of a game about building with blocks. It becomes the best-selling video game of all time.

events.title: Sri Lanka's War Ends
events.body: The army defeats the Tamil Tigers after 26 years of civil war. The UN says thousands of civilians died in the final months.

events.title: Air France 447 Vanishes
events.body: An Airbus flying from Rio to Paris crashes into the Atlantic at night, killing all 228 aboard. The black boxes are found two years later.

events.title: The Swine Flu Pandemic
events.body: The World Health Organization declares the new H1N1 flu a pandemic, the first in four decades.

events.title: Iran's Green Movement
events.body: Millions protest in Iran after President Ahmadinejad is declared re-elected. The killing of a young woman, Neda Agha-Soltan, filmed on a phone, is seen around the world.

events.title: Michael Jackson Dies
events.body: The "King of Pop" dies at fifty in Los Angeles weeks before a run of comeback concerts. Grief and record sales sweep the world.

events.title: Caster Semenya Wins Gold
events.body: Eighteen-year-old South African Caster Semenya wins the 800 metres at the world championships in Berlin — and is subjected to sex testing, the start of a long fight over the rules.

events.title: Ai Weiwei's Remembering
events.body: Ai Weiwei covers the front of Munich's Haus der Kunst with 9,000 children's backpacks spelling a grieving mother's words, in memory of the schoolchildren killed in the Sichuan earthquake.

events.title: The Copenhagen Climate Summit
events.body: World leaders meet in Copenhagen hoping to agree a successor to Kyoto. They leave with only a weak, non-binding accord.

events.title: The Burj Khalifa Opens
events.body: Dubai opens the world's tallest building, at 828 metres, in the middle of a debt crisis.

events.title: The Haiti Earthquake
events.body: An earthquake devastates Port-au-Prince. Estimates of the dead range from about 100,000 to over 200,000; a cholera epidemic follows.

events.title: Alexander McQueen Dies
events.body: The British designer, known for dark, theatrical shows, dies at forty. A retrospective of his work later breaks attendance records in New York and London.

events.title: The Ash Cloud
events.body: Iceland's Eyjafjallajökull volcano erupts under a glacier. Its ash closes most of Europe's airspace for days — the biggest air-travel shutdown since the Second World War.

events.title: Deepwater Horizon
events.body: An oil rig explodes in the Gulf of Mexico, killing eleven workers. Oil gushes from the sea floor for 87 days — the worst marine oil spill in history.

events.title: Noma Named Best in the World
events.body: A Copenhagen restaurant cooking only Nordic ingredients — moss, ants, sea buckthorn — is named the world's best, and the New Nordic movement goes global.

events.title: Africa's First World Cup
events.body: The FIFA World Cup opens in Johannesburg, the first held on African soil, to the sound of vuvuzelas. Spain win the final at Soccer City a month later.

events.title: Instagram Launches
events.body: A photo-sharing app with square frames and filters launches on the iPhone, and changes how the world sees itself.

events.title: An Empty Chair in Oslo
events.body: Jailed Chinese writer Liu Xiaobo wins the Nobel Peace Prize. At the ceremony in December, his medal is placed on an empty chair.

events.title: The Chilean Miners Rescued
events.body: All 33 miners trapped 700 metres underground for 69 days are lifted out one by one in a capsule, watched live by a billion people.

events.title: Mexican Cooking Becomes World Heritage
events.body: UNESCO recognises traditional Mexican cuisine, together with the French gastronomic meal, as Intangible Cultural Heritage — among the first food traditions on the list.

events.title: WikiLeaks Releases the Cables
events.body: WikiLeaks and five newspapers begin publishing a quarter of a million secret American diplomatic cables.

events.title: Mohamed Bouazizi
events.body: A Tunisian fruit seller sets himself alight after police confiscate his cart. His protest and death set off the uprisings known as the Arab Spring.

events.title: Tunisia's Revolution
events.body: After four weeks of protests, President Ben Ali flees Tunisia after 23 years in power. Protests spread across the Arab world.

events.title: Mubarak Falls
events.body: Eighteen days of protest centred on Cairo's Tahrir Square force Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak to resign after thirty years.

events.title: The Tōhoku Earthquake and Fukushima
events.body: The most powerful earthquake recorded in Japan sends a tsunami over the north-east coast, killing more than 18,000 people and causing meltdowns at the Fukushima nuclear plant.

events.title: Syria's War Begins
events.body: Protests in Daraa and Damascus are met with bullets. The uprising becomes a civil war that kills hundreds of thousands and drives millions from their homes.

sources.title: Deaths as Syrian forces fire on protesters (March 2011)
“We've never seen such horror”: crimes against humanity in Daraa (June 2011)

events.title: Bin Laden Killed
events.body: American special forces kill Osama bin Laden at a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan.

events.title: South Sudan Is Born
events.body: After decades of war, South Sudan becomes independent from Sudan — the world's newest country.

events.title: The Norway Attacks
events.body: A far-right extremist bombs government buildings in Oslo, then shoots 69 people, most of them teenagers, at a youth camp on the island of Utøya.

events.title: Amy Winehouse Dies
events.body: The English singer dies at 27 in London, five years after Back to Black made her a star.

events.title: Occupy Wall Street
events.body: Protesters camp in a park near Wall Street under the slogan "We are the 99%". Occupy camps spring up in hundreds of cities.

events.title: Steve Jobs Dies
events.body: The co-founder of Apple dies of cancer at 56.

events.title: Gaddafi Killed
events.body: Libya's ruler of 42 years is captured and killed by rebel fighters near his home town of Sirte.

events.title: Seven Billion People
events.body: The United Nations marks the day the world's population reaches seven billion — double what it was in 1967.

events.title: The Murals of Mohamed Mahmoud Street
events.body: Near Tahrir Square, artists cover the walls of Mohamed Mahmoud Street with portraits of the protesters killed in Egypt's revolution and the clashes that followed.

events.title: Russia's Winter Protests
events.body: Tens of thousands rally on Bolotnaya Square in Moscow against fraud in parliamentary elections — the biggest protests of the Putin years so far.

events.title: Pussy Riot's Punk Prayer
events.body: Members of a feminist punk collective perform a protest song against Putin in Moscow's main cathedral. Three are jailed for 'hooliganism'.

events.title: Alone at the Bottom of the Sea
events.body: Film director James Cameron dives alone to the Challenger Deep, nearly 11 kilometres down — only the second crewed visit to the deepest point of the ocean.

events.title: Globe to Globe
events.body: London's Globe Theatre stages all 37 of Shakespeare's plays in 37 languages, from a Shona Two Gentlemen of Verona to a Māori Troilus and Cressida.

events.title: The Higgs Boson Found
events.body: Scientists at CERN announce the discovery of a particle matching the Higgs boson, predicted almost fifty years earlier. Peter Higgs wipes away a tear.

events.title: Timbuktu's Shrines Destroyed
events.body: Islamist fighters who have seized northern Mali smash centuries-old Sufi shrines in Timbuktu, a World Heritage Site.

events.title: The London Olympics
events.body: Danny Boyle's opening ceremony tells Britain's story from the Industrial Revolution to the internet, with the NHS and the Windrush generation on stage.

events.title: Curiosity Lands on Mars
events.body: NASA lowers a car-sized rover onto Mars on a "sky crane". Curiosity finds that Gale Crater once held a lake that could have supported life.

events.title: The Marikana Massacre
events.body: South African police open fire on striking platinum miners at Marikana, killing 34. It is the deadliest police action since the end of apartheid.

events.title: Malala Shot
events.body: A Taliban gunman shoots fifteen-year-old Malala Yousafzai on her school bus in Pakistan's Swat Valley for speaking out for girls' education. She survives.

events.title: The Jump From Space
events.body: Felix Baumgartner jumps from a balloon 39 kilometres above New Mexico and breaks the sound barrier in free fall.

events.title: Hurricane Sandy
events.body: A vast storm floods New York City's subways and the Jersey Shore after sweeping through the Caribbean.

events.title: Xi Jinping Takes Charge
events.body: Xi Jinping becomes general secretary of China's Communist Party. He will become the country's most powerful leader since Mao.

events.title: Gangnam Style Hits a Billion
events.body: Psy's horse-riding dance becomes the first video to be watched a billion times on YouTube, and K-pop goes global.

events.title: Pope Francis Elected
events.body: Weeks after Benedict XVI becomes the first pope to resign in six centuries, Argentine Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio is elected — the first pope from the Americas.

events.title: The Boston Marathon Bombing
events.body: Two bombs near the finish line of the Boston Marathon kill three people and injure hundreds.

events.title: The Rana Plaza Collapse
events.body: A factory building near Dhaka that made clothes for Western brands collapses, killing more than 1,100 garment workers. Cracks had been reported the day before.

events.title: The Gezi Park Protests
events.body: A sit-in against plans to build over a park in central Istanbul grows into nationwide protests against the Turkish government.

events.title: The Snowden Revelations
events.body: Former contractor Edward Snowden leaks documents showing how much of the world's phone and internet traffic US and British spy agencies collect.

events.title: Black Lives Matter Begins
events.body: After the man who killed Black teenager Trayvon Martin is acquitted, three organisers start the hashtag #BlackLivesMatter. It becomes a movement.

events.title: The First Lab-Grown Burger
events.body: A burger grown from cow stem cells in a Dutch laboratory is cooked and tasted in London. It cost about €250,000 to make.

events.title: The Westgate Mall Attack
events.body: Al-Shabaab gunmen attack a shopping centre in Nairobi; the siege lasts four days and kills 67 people.

events.title: I Am Malala
events.body: A year after she was shot, Malala Yousafzai's memoir, written with journalist Christina Lamb, is published around the world.

events.title: Typhoon Haiyan
events.body: One of the strongest storms ever to make landfall flattens Tacloban in the Philippines. More than 6,000 people die.

events.title: Euromaidan Begins
events.body: Protests start on Kyiv's Maidan square when Ukraine's president drops a deal with the European Union. By February he has fled to Russia.

events.title: Nelson Mandela Dies
events.body: South Africa's first democratic president dies at 95 in Johannesburg. Leaders from around the world gather in Soweto's FNB Stadium to mourn him.

events.title: China Lands on the Moon
events.body: China's Chang'e 3 makes the first soft landing on the Moon since 1976 and sets the Yutu rover rolling.

events.title: MH370 Disappears
events.body: A Malaysia Airlines flight from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing vanishes with 239 people aboard. Despite the largest search in aviation history, the plane has never been found.

events.title: Russia Annexes Crimea
events.body: Weeks after unmarked Russian troops appear on the peninsula and a hurried referendum, Russia annexes Crimea from Ukraine.

events.title: The Chibok Schoolgirls
events.body: Boko Haram kidnaps 276 girls from a school in north-eastern Nigeria. #BringBackOurGirls spreads worldwide; many of the girls are still missing years later.

events.title: Fashion Revolution Day
events.body: On the first anniversary of Rana Plaza, people around the world turn their clothes inside out and ask brands: "Who made my clothes?"

events.title: Modi Becomes Prime Minister
events.body: Narendra Modi's BJP wins India's first single-party majority in thirty years.

events.title: ISIS Declares a Caliphate
events.body: Weeks after seizing Mosul, the Islamic State group declares a caliphate across parts of Iraq and Syria. It carries out massacres and the enslavement of Yazidi women.

events.title: Miners Shot Down
events.body: Rehad Desai's documentary uses police and news footage to retrace, day by day, the strike that ended in the Marikana massacre.

events.title: Germany 7, Brazil 1
events.body: Host nation Brazil are crushed 7–1 by Germany in the World Cup semi-final in Belo Horizonte.

events.title: MH17 Shot Down
events.body: A Malaysia Airlines plane is shot down over eastern Ukraine by a Russian-made missile, killing all 298 aboard.

events.title: Ebola Declared an Emergency
events.body: The WHO declares the Ebola epidemic in Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia an international emergency. More than 11,000 people die before it ends.

events.title: Ferguson
events.body: The police killing of Michael Brown, a Black eighteen-year-old, in Ferguson, Missouri, sets off months of protest.

events.title: Scotland Votes to Stay
events.body: Scotland votes 55% to 45% to remain part of the United Kingdom.

events.title: Exhibit B Cancelled
events.body: Brett Bailey's installation, in which Black performers recreate the 'human zoos' of the colonial era, is cancelled in London after protests call it racist. The debate over who may tell whose story spreads.

events.title: Hong Kong's Umbrella Movement
events.body: Police fire tear gas at protesters demanding free elections; they shield themselves with umbrellas and occupy central Hong Kong for 79 days.

events.title: Malala Wins the Nobel
events.body: At seventeen, Malala Yousafzai becomes the youngest Nobel laureate, sharing the Peace Prize with Indian child-rights campaigner Kailash Satyarthi.

events.title: Landing on a Comet
events.body: The European probe Rosetta's lander Philae touches down on a comet — bouncing twice before coming to rest in a shadow.

events.title: The Charlie Hebdo Attack
events.body: Gunmen kill twelve people at the Paris office of the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo. "Je suis Charlie" becomes a rallying cry.

events.title: To Pimp a Butterfly
events.body: Kendrick Lamar's album, steeped in jazz and funk, confronts race in America. Its song "Alright" is chanted at protests.

events.title: Rhodes Must Fall
events.body: After a month of student protest, the statue of Cecil John Rhodes is removed from the University of Cape Town. The movement for decolonisation spreads to Oxford and beyond.

events.title: The Nepal Earthquake
events.body: An earthquake near Kathmandu kills nearly 9,000 people and topples centuries-old temples, and an avalanche on Everest kills climbers at base camp.

events.title: Marriage Equality in the US
events.body: The US Supreme Court rules that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry.

events.title: Greece Says No
events.body: Greeks vote to reject the bail-out terms of their creditors. A week later the government accepts harsher terms to stay in the euro.

events.title: New Horizons at Pluto
events.body: Nine years after launch, NASA's probe flies past Pluto and sends home the first close-up pictures, including a vast heart-shaped plain.

events.title: Hamilton Opens on Broadway
events.body: Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop musical about an American founding father, cast mostly with actors of colour, opens to rapturous reviews.

events.title: Alan Kurdi
events.body: The photograph of a three-year-old Syrian boy drowned on a Turkish beach brings home the human cost of the refugee crisis. More than a million people reach Europe by sea that year.

events.title: Gravitational Waves Detected
events.body: LIGO's detectors in the US pick up ripples in space-time from two black holes colliding over a billion years ago — confirming Einstein's prediction a century on.

events.title: The Global Goals
events.body: The UN adopts seventeen Sustainable Development Goals — to end poverty and hunger and protect the planet by 2030.

events.title: A Nobel for Artemisinin
events.body: Tu Youyou wins China's first Nobel Prize in medicine, for a malaria drug she found in an ancient book of Chinese remedies. It has saved millions of lives.

events.title: A Nobel for Many Voices
events.body: Svetlana Alexievich wins the Nobel Prize in Literature for her oral histories of Soviet and post-Soviet life — including the voices of Chernobyl.

events.title: Fees Must Fall
events.body: Students shut down South African universities over fee increases. Within days the government freezes fees for 2016.

events.title: Myanmar Votes
events.body: Aung San Suu Kyi's party wins Myanmar's first openly contested election in 25 years.

events.title: The Paris Attacks
events.body: Gunmen and suicide bombers attack a concert hall, a stadium, bars and restaurants in Paris, killing 130 people. ISIS claims responsibility.

events.title: The Paris Agreement
events.body: Almost every country on Earth agrees to hold global warming well below 2°C and to try for 1.5°C.

sources.title: Highlights for Saturday, 12 December 2015
Nations adopt Paris agreement on climate change

events.title: The Zika Emergency
events.body: The WHO declares the Zika virus an emergency after a surge of babies born with small heads in north-eastern Brazil.

events.title: The Life Jackets of Berlin
events.body: Ai Weiwei wraps the columns of Berlin's Konzerthaus in about 14,000 life jackets left behind by refugees on the Greek island of Lesbos.

events.title: AlphaGo Beats Lee Sedol
events.body: Google DeepMind's program beats one of the world's best players of Go, four games to one — a decade earlier than many experts expected.

events.title: Zaha Hadid Dies
events.body: The Iraqi-born architect of swooping, futuristic buildings, the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize, dies at 65.

events.title: The Panama Papers
events.body: Journalists around the world publish 11.5 million leaked files from a Panamanian law firm, exposing how the rich and powerful hide money offshore.

events.title: Muhammad Ali Dies
events.body: The boxer who refused the Vietnam draft and called himself "the greatest" dies at 74.

events.title: Brexit
events.body: The United Kingdom votes 52% to 48% to leave the European Union.

sources.title: Brexit: Britain votes to leave EU in historic divorce (24 June 2016)
How the Brexit result unfolded

events.title: Pokémon Go
events.body: An augmented-reality game sends millions of people out into the streets to catch Pokémon on their phones.

events.title: Harry Potter and the Cursed Child
events.body: A two-part stage sequel set nineteen years after the books opens in London's West End.

events.title: The First Refugee Olympic Team
events.body: At the Rio Olympics, ten athletes who have fled their countries compete under the Olympic flag. One, Syrian swimmer Yusra Mardini, had pushed a sinking dinghy to Lesbos.

events.title: A Nobel for Bob Dylan
events.body: The Nobel Prize in Literature goes to a songwriter for the first time, "for having created new poetic expressions within the great American song tradition".

events.title: Trump Elected
events.body: Businessman and television personality Donald Trump wins the US presidency, losing the popular vote but winning the electoral college.

events.title: Peace in Colombia
events.body: Colombia's government and the FARC guerrillas sign a revised peace deal, ending a 52-year war. President Santos wins the Nobel Peace Prize.

events.title: Fidel Castro Dies
events.body: The leader of the Cuban revolution dies at 90 in Havana.

events.title: The Fall of Aleppo
events.body: After a long siege and heavy bombing, Syrian government forces retake all of Aleppo, once the country's largest city.

events.title: The Women's March
events.body: The day after Trump's inauguration, millions march in Washington and cities around the world for women's rights.

events.title: Macron Elected
events.body: Emmanuel Macron, 39, defeats far-right candidate Marine Le Pen to become the youngest president in French history.

events.title: The Grenfell Tower Fire
events.body: Fire races up the cladding of a London tower block, killing 72 people. Residents had warned about safety for years.

events.title: Colliding Neutron Stars
events.body: Gravitational-wave detectors and some seventy telescopes watch the same collision of two neutron stars — and see gold and platinum being made.

events.title: The Rohingya Flee Myanmar
events.body: A military crackdown in Rakhine State drives more than 700,000 Rohingya Muslims into Bangladesh. UN investigators later call for genocide charges.

events.title: Hurricane Maria
events.body: Maria devastates Puerto Rico, knocking out its power grid for months. Researchers later estimate about 3,000 deaths.

events.title: Zeitz MOCAA Opens
events.body: A museum of contemporary African art opens in Cape Town inside a historic grain silo, its concrete tubes carved into a cathedral-like atrium.

events.title: The Catalan Referendum
events.body: Catalonia holds an independence vote that Spain's courts have banned. Police raid polling stations; the region's declaration of independence weeks later is suspended.

events.title: #MeToo
events.body: After reports on film producer Harvey Weinstein, millions of women share experiences of sexual harassment and assault under the phrase Tarana Burke began using in 2006.

events.title: Mugabe Resigns
events.body: A week after the army takes control, Robert Mugabe resigns after 37 years ruling Zimbabwe. Crowds celebrate in Harare.

events.title: Cape Town's Day Zero
events.body: After three years of drought, Cape Town warns that its taps may run dry. Residents cut use to 50 litres a day, and Day Zero is averted.

events.title: Ramaphosa Becomes President
events.body: Jacob Zuma resigns under pressure from his own party amid corruption scandals, and Parliament elects Cyril Ramaphosa as South Africa's president.

events.title: Black Panther
events.body: A superhero film with a mostly Black cast, set in an imagined African nation that was never colonised, earns over a billion dollars worldwide.

events.title: Marielle Franco Killed
events.body: Rio de Janeiro councillor Marielle Franco, a Black, gay woman from the favelas who campaigned against police violence, is shot dead in her car.

events.title: Stephen Hawking Dies
events.body: The physicist who studied black holes and the origins of the universe — and wrote A Brief History of Time — dies in Cambridge at 76.

events.title: Cambridge Analytica
events.body: Newspapers reveal that a political consultancy harvested data from tens of millions of Facebook users without their consent.

events.title: Virgil Abloh at Louis Vuitton
events.body: Streetwear designer Virgil Abloh becomes the first Black artistic director of Louis Vuitton menswear.

events.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea Make Peace
events.body: Ethiopia's new prime minister, Abiy Ahmed, and Eritrea's president declare an end to twenty years of war and standoff.

events.title: The Thai Cave Rescue
events.body: Divers bring out the last of twelve boys and their football coach, trapped for over two weeks in the flooded Tham Luang cave.

events.title: France Win the World Cup
events.body: France beat Croatia 4–2 in the final in Moscow. Teenager Kylian Mbappé scores in the final.

events.title: Greta's School Strike
events.body: Fifteen-year-old Greta Thunberg sits outside the Swedish parliament with a sign reading "School strike for climate". Millions of students follow her lead.

events.title: Jamal Khashoggi Killed
events.body: Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi is murdered inside his country's consulate in Istanbul.

events.title: Girl with Balloon Shreds Itself
events.body: Moments after Banksy's painting sells at Sotheby's in London for over a million pounds, a shredder hidden in the frame cuts it half to pieces. It is renamed Love Is in the Bin.

events.title: The Yellow Vests
events.body: Protests over a fuel tax in France, by people wearing high-visibility vests, grow into months of weekly demonstrations against the cost of living.

events.title: Gene-Edited Babies
events.body: Chinese scientist He Jiankui announces the birth of twin girls whose DNA he edited as embryos. Scientists worldwide condemn it, and he is jailed.

events.title: Sudan's Bread Protests
events.body: A tripling of the price of bread sets off protests in the town of Atbara. They spread across Sudan and grow into a revolution.

events.title: The 737 MAX Grounded
events.body: An Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 737 MAX crashes after take-off from Addis Ababa, killing all 157 aboard — the second crash of the new model in five months. The plane is grounded worldwide.

events.title: The Christchurch Mosque Attacks
events.body: A white-supremacist gunman kills 51 people at two mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand. Within a month, the country bans most semi-automatic weapons.

events.title: The Woman in White
events.body: Lana Haroun photographs a young woman, Alaa Salah, in a white robe, leading chants from the roof of a car at the sit-in in Khartoum. The picture becomes the icon of Sudan's revolution.

events.title: The First Picture of a Black Hole
events.body: The Event Horizon Telescope, linking radio dishes across the planet, shows the shadow of the black hole at the heart of the galaxy M87.

events.title: Bashir Falls
events.body: After four months of protest, Sudan's army removes Omar al-Bashir, who had ruled for thirty years.

events.title: Notre-Dame Burns
events.body: Fire destroys the roof and spire of Paris's Notre-Dame cathedral as crowds watch in tears. It reopens, restored, in December 2024.

events.title: The Kilogram Redefined
events.body: The kilogram stops being defined by a metal cylinder kept near Paris and is defined instead by a constant of nature.

events.title: The Hong Kong Protests
events.body: Huge marches against a law allowing extradition to mainland China grow into months of protest; Beijing answers with a sweeping security law in 2020.

events.title: Toni Morrison Dies
events.body: The author of Beloved, the first Black woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, dies at 88.

events.title: The Amazon Burns
events.body: Fires set to clear land for farming burn across the Brazilian Amazon at the highest rate in a decade, bringing global outrage.

events.title: The Global Climate Strike
events.body: Millions of people, many of them school pupils, strike for climate action in more than 150 countries.

events.title: A Nobel for Abiy Ahmed
events.body: Ethiopia's prime minister wins the Nobel Peace Prize for making peace with Eritrea. A year later his country is at war in Tigray.

events.title: Quantum Supremacy Claimed
events.body: Google says its quantum processor has done in minutes a calculation that would take the fastest supercomputer thousands of years. Rivals dispute the claim.

events.title: The Springboks Win in Japan
events.body: Siya Kolisi, the Springboks' first Black Test captain, lifts the Rugby World Cup in Yokohama after South Africa beat England 32–12.

events.title: Black Summer
events.body: Bushfires burn across south-eastern Australia from late 2019, destroying thousands of homes; scientists estimate some three billion animals were killed or displaced.

events.title: A New Virus in Wuhan
events.body: China tells the WHO about a cluster of pneumonia cases of unknown cause in Wuhan. Within weeks the new coronavirus is spreading worldwide.

events.title: Brexit Happens
events.body: The United Kingdom formally leaves the European Union, three and a half years after the referendum.

events.title: COVID-19 Declared a Pandemic
events.body: The World Health Organization declares the new coronavirus a pandemic. Within weeks, half of humanity is under some form of lockdown.

sources.title: WHO Director-General's opening remarks, 11 March 2020
COVID-19 'can be characterised as a pandemic': WHO chief

events.title: The Olympics Postponed
events.body: For the first time in peacetime, the Olympic Games are put off — Tokyo 2020 moves to 2021.

events.title: South Africa Locks Down
events.body: South Africa enters one of the world's strictest lockdowns, with soldiers on the streets and a ban on alcohol and cigarette sales.

events.title: The Pandemic Is a Portal
events.body: Arundhati Roy writes that the pandemic is "a gateway between one world and the next", and asks what we choose to carry through it. The essay is read and shared around the world.

events.title: George Floyd Murdered
events.body: A Minneapolis police officer kneels on the neck of George Floyd for over nine minutes, killing him. Protests spread across the US and around the world.

sources.title: Step by step, here's how George Floyd's fatal encounter with police unfolded
What we know about George Floyd's death in Minneapolis police custody

events.title: Private Rocket, Public Crew
events.body: SpaceX launches two NASA astronauts to the ISS — the first crewed flight from American soil since the Shuttle, and the first by a private company.

events.title: Colston Toppled
events.body: Black Lives Matter protesters in Bristol pull down the statue of 17th-century slave trader Edward Colston and roll it into the harbour.

events.title: George Floyd in Idlib
events.body: Syrian artist Aziz Asmar paints a mural of George Floyd on a wall of a bombed building in Idlib, linking his death to Syria's own suffering.

events.title: Jerusalema
events.body: Master KG and Nomcebo Zikode's gospel-house song sets off a dance challenge copied by nurses, police and monks around the world in the year of lockdown.

events.title: The Beirut Explosion
events.body: Thousands of tonnes of ammonium nitrate stored for years at Beirut's port explode, killing more than 200 people and wrecking much of the city.

events.title: #EndSARS and Lekki
events.body: After two weeks of youth-led protests against a brutal police unit, soldiers open fire on peaceful protesters at the Lekki toll gate in Lagos.

events.title: War in Tigray
events.body: Fighting breaks out between Ethiopia's government and the ruling party of the Tigray region. The two-year war brings famine and mass killing.

events.title: Biden Wins
events.body: Four days after the vote, Joe Biden is projected the winner of the US presidential election. Donald Trump refuses to concede.

events.title: The First Vaccine Jab
events.body: A 90-year-old woman in Coventry becomes the first person in the world to receive an approved COVID-19 vaccine outside a trial, less than a year after the virus was identified.

events.title: The Capitol Stormed
events.body: Supporters of Donald Trump break into the US Capitol to stop Congress certifying Joe Biden's victory.

events.title: The Myanmar Coup
events.body: Myanmar's army seizes power and detains Aung San Suu Kyi. Mass protests are met with killings, and the country slides into civil war.

events.title: Perseverance Lands on Mars
events.body: NASA's rover lands in Jezero Crater to look for signs of ancient life; two months later its small helicopter, Ingenuity, makes the first powered flight on another planet.

events.title: The Ever Given
events.body: A giant container ship runs aground across the Suez Canal, blocking one of the world's busiest trade routes for six days.

events.title: The July Unrest
events.body: After former president Jacob Zuma is jailed for contempt of court, riots and looting sweep KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng. More than 350 people die.

events.title: The Tokyo Olympics
events.body: A year late and almost without spectators, the Tokyo Olympics open under pandemic rules.

events.title: The Taliban Return
events.body: As American troops withdraw, the Taliban sweep back into Kabul. Thousands crowd the airport trying to leave.

events.title: Bitcoin as Legal Tender
events.body: El Salvador becomes the first country to make Bitcoin official money.

events.title: Squid Game
events.body: A South Korean drama about debt-ridden people playing deadly children's games becomes the most watched series in Netflix's history.

events.title: A Nobel for Abdulrazak Gurnah
events.body: Zanzibar-born novelist Abdulrazak Gurnah wins the Nobel Prize in Literature for his writing on colonialism and the fate of refugees.

events.title: The Glasgow Climate Pact
events.body: The COP26 summit ends with the first climate deal to mention coal by name — softened at the last minute from "phase out" to "phase down".

events.title: South Africa Spots Omicron
events.body: Scientists in South Africa and Botswana identify a new, highly mutated coronavirus variant and alert the world. Many countries respond with travel bans on southern Africa.

events.title: Barbados Becomes a Republic
events.body: Barbados removes the Queen as head of state and becomes a republic, with Rihanna named a national hero at the ceremony.

events.title: The James Webb Telescope Launches
events.body: The largest space telescope ever built lifts off from French Guiana to look back to the first galaxies.

events.title: Desmond Tutu Dies
events.body: The archbishop who named South Africa "the Rainbow Nation" and chaired its Truth Commission dies in Cape Town at 90.

events.title: Hunga Tonga Erupts
events.body: An undersea volcano in Tonga erupts with the biggest explosion recorded in more than a century. Its shock wave circles the Earth several times.

events.title: Wordle
events.body: A free word-guessing game, made by a software engineer for his partner, spreads by shared grids of green and yellow squares. The New York Times buys it at the end of the month.

events.title: Russia Invades Ukraine
events.body: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Kyiv holds; the largest war in Europe since 1945 begins.

sources.title: Putin shatters peace in Europe as Russia invades Ukraine (24 February 2022)
February 24, 2022: the day Russia invaded Ukraine

events.title: A Pritzker for Francis Kéré
events.body: Burkinabé architect Francis Kéré, who built a school for his home village of Gando from local clay, becomes the first African to win architecture's highest prize.

events.title: Ukraine Wins Eurovision
events.body: Kalush Orchestra win the Eurovision Song Contest in Turin with "Stefania", a song for the singer's mother that becomes a wartime anthem.

events.title: Roe v. Wade Overturned
events.body: The US Supreme Court ends the constitutional right to abortion that had stood since 1973.

events.title: Webb's First Pictures
events.body: The James Webb Space Telescope sends back its first images, among them the deepest view of the universe ever taken.

events.title: The Black Sea Grain Deal
events.body: Ukraine and Russia, through Turkey and the UN, agree to let grain ships leave Ukraine's ports, easing a global food crisis caused by the war.

events.title: The Pakistan Floods
events.body: Record monsoon rains put about a third of Pakistan under water, affecting 33 million people.

events.title: Queen Elizabeth II Dies
events.body: Britain's longest-reigning monarch dies at Balmoral, aged 96, after seventy years on the throne. Her son becomes King Charles III.

events.title: Woman, Life, Freedom
events.body: Mahsa Amini, 22, dies in the custody of Iran's morality police after being arrested over her headscarf. Women-led protests sweep the country.

events.title: Baraye
events.body: Shervin Hajipour sets tweets about why people are protesting to music. "Baraye" ("For…") is viewed tens of millions of times before he is arrested; it becomes the anthem of the protests.

events.title: Eight Billion People
events.body: The UN marks the world's population passing eight billion, eleven years after it passed seven.

events.title: Banksy in Borodianka
events.body: Banksy paints a gymnast balancing on rubble on a bombed building in Borodianka, near Kyiv, and other murals in towns damaged by the Russian invasion.

events.title: ChatGPT
events.body: OpenAI releases a chatbot to the public. It reaches 100 million users in two months, and the race for artificial intelligence takes off.

events.title: Fusion Ignition
events.body: A California laboratory fires lasers at a pellet of hydrogen and, for the first time, gets more energy out of the fusion reaction than the lasers put in.

events.title: Messi's World Cup
events.body: In the first World Cup held in the Arab world, Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3–3 draw. Lionel Messi finally wins the trophy.

events.title: The Turkey–Syria Earthquakes
events.body: Two huge earthquakes hours apart strike south-eastern Turkey and northern Syria, killing more than 50,000 people.

events.title: Sudan's New War
events.body: Fighting breaks out in Khartoum between Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. It becomes one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

events.title: India Overtakes China
events.body: UN figures show India has become the most populous country on Earth.

events.title: A Coronation
events.body: Charles III is crowned at Westminster Abbey, the first British coronation in seventy years.

events.title: The Titan Submersible
events.body: A small private submersible taking tourists to the wreck of the Titanic implodes, killing all five aboard.

events.title: The Wagner Mutiny
events.body: Mercenary chief Yevgeny Prigozhin seizes Rostov-on-Don and marches on Moscow, then turns back. Two months later he dies in a plane crash.

events.title: Hollywood Actors Strike
events.body: Actors join striking writers, shutting down American film and television for months — partly over the use of artificial intelligence.

events.title: Spain Win the Women's World Cup
events.body: Spain beat England in Sydney. The federation president's unwanted kiss on a player at the medal ceremony sets off a national reckoning: "Se acabó" — it's over.

events.title: BRICS Grows in Johannesburg
events.body: At a summit in Johannesburg, the BRICS group of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa invites six more countries to join.

events.title: India Lands Near the Moon's South Pole
events.body: Chandrayaan-3 makes India the fourth country to land softly on the Moon, and the first near its south pole.

events.title: The Morocco Earthquake
events.body: An earthquake in the High Atlas mountains kills nearly 3,000 people and destroys mountain villages and historic buildings near Marrakesh.

events.title: The Derna Floods
events.body: Storm Daniel bursts two dams above the Libyan city of Derna, sweeping whole neighbourhoods into the sea. Thousands die.

events.title: The October 7 Attack
events.body: Hamas-led fighters attack southern Israel, killing about 1,200 people and taking some 250 hostages into Gaza.

events.title: The War in Gaza
events.body: Israel launches a ground invasion of Gaza after weeks of bombing. Over the following two years, tens of thousands of Palestinians are killed and most of Gaza is destroyed.

sources.title: Israel–Hamas war live, 27 October 2023
Ground battles rage in Gaza as communications are cut

events.title: South Africa Takes Israel to the ICJ
events.body: South Africa files a case at the International Court of Justice accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza. In January the court orders Israel to prevent genocidal acts.

events.title: The Great North American Eclipse
events.body: A total solar eclipse crosses Mexico, the United States and Canada, watched by tens of millions.

events.title: The ANC Loses Its Majority
events.body: Thirty years after 1994, South Africa's ANC wins only about 40% of the vote. It forms a Government of National Unity with nine other parties, including the DA.

events.title: Mexico Elects a Woman
events.body: Claudia Sheinbaum, a climate scientist and former mayor of Mexico City, wins a landslide to become Mexico's first woman president.

events.title: India's Giant Election
events.body: Results come in from the largest election in history, with more than 640 million votes cast. Modi wins a third term but loses his party's majority.

events.title: Kenya's Gen Z Protests
events.body: Young Kenyans organising online storm parliament over tax rises in a finance bill. Police kill dozens; the president withdraws the bill.

events.title: The CrowdStrike Outage
events.body: A faulty security update crashes about 8.5 million Windows computers, grounding flights and closing hospitals and banks around the world.

events.title: The Paris Olympics
events.body: The Olympics open with athletes floating down the Seine on boats, the first opening ceremony held outside a stadium.

events.title: Bangladesh's Student Revolution
events.body: After weeks of student-led protest in which hundreds are killed, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina flees to India. Muhammad Yunus leads an interim government.

events.title: A Nobel for AlphaFold
events.body: Demis Hassabis and John Jumper of Google DeepMind share the Nobel Prize in Chemistry with David Baker for predicting and designing the shapes of proteins.

events.title: A Nobel for Han Kang
events.body: South Korean novelist Han Kang wins the Nobel Prize in Literature, for prose that "confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of human life".

events.title: The Booster Caught
events.body: SpaceX catches a returning Starship booster in the giant mechanical arms of its launch tower in Texas.

events.title: The Valencia Floods
events.body: Torrential rain sends flash floods through towns around Valencia in Spain, killing more than 220 people.

events.title: Trump Elected Again
events.body: Donald Trump wins a second, non-consecutive term as US president.

events.title: ICC Warrants for Netanyahu
events.body: The International Criminal Court issues arrest warrants for Israel's prime minister and former defence minister, and for a Hamas commander, over the war in Gaza.

events.title: Martial Law in Seoul
events.body: South Korea's President Yoon declares martial law; lawmakers climb fences to reach parliament and vote it down within hours. He is impeached and later removed.

events.title: Assad Falls
events.body: Rebels sweep into Damascus in eleven days and Bashar al-Assad flees to Moscow, ending his family's 53-year rule of Syria.

events.title: The Los Angeles Fires
events.body: Wind-driven wildfires burn through Pacific Palisades and Altadena, destroying more than 16,000 buildings.

events.title: Trump Returns
events.body: Donald Trump is sworn in again. Sweeping tariffs and cuts to foreign aid follow within months.

events.title: The DeepSeek Shock
events.body: A Chinese start-up's AI model, said to be built for a fraction of American costs, tops app charts and wipes hundreds of billions off US chip stocks in a day.

events.title: The Myanmar Earthquake
events.body: A magnitude-7.7 earthquake near Mandalay kills thousands in war-torn Myanmar, and brings down a skyscraper under construction in Bangkok.

events.title: Pope Francis Dies
events.body: The first pope from the Americas dies on Easter Monday, a day after greeting crowds in St Peter's Square.

events.title: India and Pakistan Clash
events.body: Two weeks after gunmen kill 26 people, most of them tourists, at Pahalgam in Kashmir, India strikes targets in Pakistan. Four days of missile and drone attacks end in a ceasefire.

events.title: Pope Leo XIV
events.body: American-born Robert Prevost, who spent much of his life as a missionary and bishop in Peru, is elected the first pope from the United States.

events.title: South Korea Elects Lee Jae-myung
events.body: Six months after the martial-law crisis, South Koreans elect opposition leader Lee Jae-myung as president.

events.title: The Twelve-Day War
events.body: Israel attacks Iran's nuclear sites and military leaders; Iran fires missiles at Israel. The US bombs Iranian nuclear plants before a ceasefire twelve days later.

events.title: The Gaza Ceasefire
events.body: Three days after a ceasefire takes effect, Hamas frees the last 20 living Israeli hostages and Israel releases nearly 2,000 Palestinian prisoners.

events.title: The Louvre Jewel Heist
events.body: In about four minutes on a Sunday morning, thieves use a furniture lift to reach the Louvre's Galerie d'Apollon and escape with French crown jewels.

events.title: Hurricane Melissa
events.body: One of the strongest Atlantic hurricanes on record hits Jamaica as a Category 5 storm, then Cuba, leaving dozens dead across the Caribbean.

events.title: COP30 in the Amazon
events.body: The UN climate summit meets in Belém, at the mouth of the Amazon, ten years after the Paris Agreement.

events.title: The G20 in Johannesburg
events.body: South Africa hosts the first G20 summit held in Africa. Leaders adopt a declaration on climate, debt and inequality despite a US boycott.

events.title: Milan–Cortina Winter Olympics
events.body: The Winter Olympics open in Milan, spread across venues in northern Italy's cities and mountains.

events.title: Artemis II Flies Around the Moon
events.body: Four astronauts launch from Florida on the first crewed voyage to the Moon since 1972. Over ten days they fly around its far side — further from Earth than anyone before — and splash down off San Diego on 10 April.

events.title: The World Cup Opens in Mexico City
events.body: The first 48-team World Cup, shared by Mexico, the United States and Canada, opens at the Estadio Azteca — the first stadium to stage matches at three World Cups.

events.title: Spain Win the World Cup
events.body: Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time in the final near New York, with a goal from Ferran Torres, to win their second World Cup.
